citation: 'Kusken Kalén' ('Kalén the coachman'). Glass negative by Ernst Blom. Västmanlands läns museum, Västerås, Vlm-Blom P 157.
author: Ernst Blom (photographer)
repository: Västmanlands läns museum, Västerås, Sweden, Vlm-Blom P 157, glass negative (DigitaltMuseum 021017894192; K-samsök http://kulturarvsdata.se/S-UVLM/photo/Vlm-BlomP157). Image server copy 1889 x 3000 px (WebP), saved here as JPEG at the same size.
locator: The whole negative; a standing three-quarter-length portrait. His face, turned slightly to his left, is at x 895-1135, y 650-890 (about 240 px across, cap brim to chin).
rights_note: Västmanlands läns museum marks the image Public Domain Mark 1.0 (K-samsök mediaLicense 'pdmark'; Europeana edmRights PDM 1.0). If the negative is from the 1920s rather than earlier, the museum's mark is still the stated status; under Swedish law a simple photographic picture made before 1969 is out of protection.
access_notes: Found 2026-11-07 through the Europeana API (record /133/S_UVLM_photo_Vlm_BlomP157) and K-samsök (which has no date, place or description beyond the title and the photographer). Image fetched from ems.dimu.org at dimension=4000x4000, which returned 1889 x 3000. digitaltmuseum.se answered 403. A better-dated but too-small alternative: 'Peter Andersson, kusk på Härlingstorp, Axvall', Werner Lindhe, 1904, Västergötlands museum 1M16-B145188:182 (363 x 543 px; face about 80 px). Another: 'Kusken Carl August Andersson (1851-1943)' with the stallion Bayard at Björksund, 1904, Sörmlands museum SLM 413620 (CC0) - exactly the right age and year, but full-length beside a horse (face about 25 px) and the museum's image host refused connections from this container.
note: THIS IS NOT CHARLES NELSON. No photograph of Charles Nelson was found. Kalén stands in for him because he was a Swedish coachman - the record's title names him as one, and he wears a coachman's livery coat and crowned cap - and by appearance a man of middle age, as Charles Nelson was in 1904 (56; born June 1848 in Sweden, came to the US 1871; the Glessners' coachman, 1880 and 1900 censuses). The record gives no date, no first name and no age: the age is a reading of the picture. Ernst Blom's dated negatives in the same museum are mostly 1920s-1930s, so this one may be later than 1904. A studio glass-negative portrait of a man standing in front of a painted backdrop, in a dark peaked cap with a crown badge and an S-like monogram, a dark double-row buttoned livery tunic with piped cape collar, and light breeches. His face: deep-set eyes under heavy brows, a long straight nose, prominent cheekbones, a very large waxed moustache with upturned ends, short hair at the temples; lined, middle-aged. The negative has some emulsion damage at the edges and a few spots, none on the face.
what_it_supplies: the proportions of a middle-aged Swedish coachman's face, near frontal
how a Swedish private coachman's livery, cap and moustache looked
what_it_does_not_supply: Charles Nelson's face, his colouring, or anything about him
a date for the photograph or the sitter's age
